[INSTRUMENTAL — TAR SHEHNAI ONLY]
Every sound comes from tar shehnai. Layer multiple performances when polyphony is needed. Use bowed melody strings, sympathetic resonance, drones, double-stops, rhythmic bowing and the attached metal horn.

[INTRO — FROM RESONANCE]
Begin almost inaudibly with a low sustained bowed tone. Let sympathetic strings awaken around it. Add overlapping sustained pitches until layered tar shehnai resembles a dark mechanical organ. Reveal a minor progression slowly, with harmonic-minor tension. Increase bow pressure, resonance and horn projection until the sound becomes physically imposing.

[PRIMARY MOTIF — 4/4]
Collapse the sustained texture into a hard rhythmic bowed figure. Build a heavy riff from repeated pedal tones, short aggressive bow strokes, double-stops and low-register accents. The bowing supplies the pulse. Begin simply; on each return add galloping subdivisions, slides into important notes, brief high answers and sympathetic-string after-ring. Use harmonic minor prominently, including a major dominant created by the raised leading tone.

[MELODIC LEAD]
Keep a low repeated foundation while another tar shehnai layer becomes the lead voice. Use long meend, narrow pitch inflections, rapid ornaments and high sustained notes. Introduce a flattened second near the end for Phrygian bite. Supporting layers displace accents enough to blur beat 1 while remaining in 4/4.

[DENSE RHYTHMIC PASS]
Layer low ostinato, short double-stopped attacks, resonant sustained tones and answering melodic fragments. Make one instrument sound improbably large without hiding its acoustic identity.

[LEAD IMPROVISATION I]
High tar shehnai takes a long solo over the repeating bowed pulse. Alternate long crying notes with quick ornaments and sudden bursts of rapid playing. Lower layers become progressively busier.

[TRANSITION]
Break apart the established riff. Move through descending harmonies with broken bowed attacks and syncopated pulses. Introduce triplets, thin the texture, then let the aggressive 4/4 machinery disappear.

[MIDSECTION — F# MINOR — 6/8]
Enter a radically more spacious world. A low layer outlines roots, fifths and octaves while sympathetic strings ring clearly. Above it, play a simple lyrical melody with a different ornamental fill at each phrase ending. Use slides, restrained vibrato and natural resonance. Leave real space between phrases. The mood is immense and uncanny, not sentimental.

[ARPEGGIATED EXPANSION]
Gradually turn the accompaniment into flowing arpeggios. Begin sparsely, then layer complementary figures in different registers. Let sympathetic resonance overlap phrases. Increase density until the instrument seems to generate a web of interacting strings. Turn some arpeggios into rapid galloping bowed figures while staying in 6/8.

[QUIET CLEARING]
Strip back to one low pattern and one exposed high melodic line.

[EXTENDED TAR SHEHNAI SOLO]
Move fully into the upper register. Use rapid ornaments, left-hand articulation, fast scalar fragments, arpeggios, wide slides, repeated notes, sustained cries and abrupt register changes. Add occasional harmonized tar shehnai layers. Build until the whole 20-string resonant system seems activated and the horn-projected upper register becomes almost painfully bright.

[HEAVY REPRISE — 4/4]
Snap back to the opening tonal world. Return to the aggressive bowed pedal motif, altered rather than copied. Combine accumulated ideas: gallops, slides, triplets, high answering phrases, double-stops and sustained resonance.

[OUTRO — CONTINUOUS INVENTION]
Do not end with a neat cadence. Keep the primary rhythmic figure moving while upper-register fills become increasingly wild: rapid ornaments, slides, scale fragments and new melodic variants. Begin a long natural fade. Continue inventing new phrases beneath the fade rather than merely repeating. Let sympathetic strings and horn resonance become the final audible elements.

Guitars enter as atmosphere first, then harden into the riff.

Bass initially drives straight, forceful eighth notes beneath the guitars.
Keep the tonal center dark; use a minor harmony that briefly turns its dominant from minor to major to expose the raised leading tone.
With each return, mutate the bass part: add galloping 16ths, short slides into the tonic, syncopated pickups and small rhythmic deviations.
Drums stay in 4/4 but use displaced crashes/snare accents so the listener occasionally loses where beat 1 is.

[LEAD BASS PASS]
Keep the guitar harmony relatively simple while the bass stops behaving like accompaniment and becomes a lead voice.
Write a lyrical, muscular upper-register bass melody over the progression.
Toward the end, introduce a flattened 2nd for a sharp Phrygian bite.
Let drums continue shifting accents around the bar without actually changing meter.

[FULL-BAND ROCKED-OUT PASS]
Whole band unifies around the same harmonic material at greater intensity.
Bass remains fingerstyle and aggressive.
Use a descending heavy figure and let the bass keep changing its articulation rather than looping identically.
Return to the main riff with another fresh bass variation.

[GUITAR SOLO I]
Long expressive guitar solo over the galloping heavy foundation.
Rhythm section remains disciplined and repetitive enough to make the solo feel airborne.
Bass alternates pedal-tone eighths with gallops and occasional slides.

[TRANSITION DEVELOPMENT]
Break the established pattern.
Move through a descending power-chord sequence with broken/syncopated eighth notes.
Introduce triplet figures.
Reduce and reconfigure the harmony until the entire character of the piece is ready to change.

[MIDSECTION — sudden key + meter shift — F# MINOR — 6/8]
Drop into a spacious, luminous 6/8 section.
This must feel like entering a vast open interior after the compressed heavy opening.
Bass carries a beautiful root–5th–octave framework with a different melodic fill at the end of nearly every phrase.
Keep the fills related but never identical.
Lean toward minor pentatonic color rather than harmonic-minor severity.
Layer clean or lightly driven guitar harmonies above it.
Let the section breathe and build for a long time.

[ARPEGGIATED BUILD]
Gradually convert the guitar harmony into interlocking arpeggios.
Then flip the orchestration: bass also becomes arpeggiated and more animated.
Increase rhythmic density by turning some arpeggios into galloping figures.
Layer harmonized lines until bass and guitars feel braided together.
Do not resolve too early.

[GUITAR SOLO II — restrained foundation]
Place a melodic guitar solo over a simpler, root-heavy bass foundation.
This is a short clearing before the central bass feature.

Move the spotlight entirely to upper-register electric bass.
Technically demanding but melodic: hammer-ons, pull-offs, rhythmic fragments, fast arpeggios, position shifts and harmonized overdub-like lines.
Let the harmony roam through related minor arpeggios while preserving a strong tonal center.

Build to a clear peak, then snap back into the heavy world.

[HEAVY REPRISE + FINAL GUITAR SOLO]
Return abruptly to the crushing riff language.
Add one more guitar solo while bass begins comparatively simple, then grows more restless.
Bring back earlier motifs in altered form so the ending feels cumulative rather than repeated.

[OUTRO — FADE WITH ESCALATING BASS FILLS]
Band keeps driving as the track fades rather than ending cleanly.

[INSTRUMENTAL — NO VOCALS]

[INTRO — distant, slow reveal]
Begin almost from silence with heavily effected electric bass alone.
Bass should feel organ-like: sustained, layered, resonant, slightly eerie.
Let a dark minor-key progression emerge gradually, with harmonic-minor tension.
Increase volume and density in stages; do not rush the reveal.
Guitars enter as atmosphere first, then harden into the riff.

[MAIN RIFF — 4/4]
Lock into a massive mid-tempo heavy riff.
Bass initially drives straight, forceful eighth notes beneath the guitars.
Keep the tonal center dark; use a minor harmony that briefly turns its dominant from minor to major to expose the raised leading tone.
With each return, mutate the bass part: add galloping 16ths, short slides into the tonic, syncopated pickups and small rhythmic deviations.
Drums stay in 4/4 but use displaced crashes/snare accents so the listener occasionally loses where beat 1 is.

[LEAD BASS PASS]
Keep the guitar harmony relatively simple while the bass stops behaving like accompaniment and becomes a lead voice.
Write a lyrical, muscular upper-register bass melody over the progression.
Toward the end, introduce a flattened 2nd for a sharp Phrygian bite.
Let drums continue shifting accents around the bar without actually changing meter.

[FULL-BAND ROCKED-OUT PASS]
Whole band unifies around the same harmonic material at greater intensity.
Bass remains fingerstyle and aggressive.
Use a descending heavy figure and let the bass keep changing its articulation rather than looping identically.
Return to the main riff with another fresh bass variation.

[GUITAR SOLO I]
Long expressive guitar solo over the galloping heavy foundation.
Rhythm section remains disciplined and repetitive enough to make the solo feel airborne.
Bass alternates pedal-tone eighths with gallops and occasional slides.

[TRANSITION DEVELOPMENT]
Break the established pattern.
Move through a descending power-chord sequence with broken/syncopated eighth notes.
Introduce triplet figures.
Reduce and reconfigure the harmony until the entire character of the piece is ready to change.

[MIDSECTION — sudden key + meter shift — F# MINOR — 6/8]
Drop into a spacious, luminous 6/8 section.
This must feel like entering a vast open interior after the compressed heavy opening.
Bass carries a beautiful root–5th–octave framework with a different melodic fill at the end of nearly every phrase.
Keep the fills related but never identical.
Lean toward minor pentatonic color rather than harmonic-minor severity.
Layer clean or lightly driven guitar harmonies above it.
Let the section breathe and build for a long time.

[ARPEGGIATED BUILD]
Gradually convert the guitar harmony into interlocking arpeggios.
Then flip the orchestration: bass also becomes arpeggiated and more animated.
Increase rhythmic density by turning some arpeggios into galloping figures.
Layer harmonized lines until bass and guitars feel braided together.
Do not resolve too early.

[GUITAR SOLO II — restrained foundation]
Place a melodic guitar solo over a simpler, root-heavy bass foundation.
This is a short clearing before the central bass feature.

[EPIC BASS SOLO]
Move the spotlight entirely to upper-register electric bass.
Technically demanding but melodic: hammer-ons, pull-offs, rhythmic fragments, fast arpeggios, position shifts and harmonized overdub-like lines.
Let the harmony roam through related minor arpeggios while preserving a strong tonal center.
The bass should sound capable of occupying the expressive territory normally reserved for lead guitar.
Build to a clear peak, then snap back into the heavy world.

[HEAVY REPRISE + FINAL GUITAR SOLO]
Return abruptly to the crushing riff language.
Add one more guitar solo while bass begins comparatively simple, then grows more restless.
Bring back earlier motifs in altered form so the ending feels cumulative rather than repeated.

[OUTRO — FADE WITH ESCALATING BASS FILLS]
Band keeps driving as the track fades rather than ending cleanly.
Under the fade, let the bass become increasingly unruly: rapid hammer-on figures, scale fragments, upper-register fills, slides and technically difficult variations that were not heard earlier.
The last impression should be that the bass is still inventing new material after the listener can barely hear it.

Hi, nice to meet you, I’m Nathan McKnight—just in from Ohio,  
doing post-doc work in Gothoslavic dialectal and historiographic reconstruction.

Vítám vás, Nathan; it’s always good to see Gothoslavic studies reaching  
all the way out to the American Midwest. You’ve arrived at a sharp time for the field,  
as we’re trying to pull apart the “monolithic” view of the BohoBasin  
that lingers in older, essentialist surveys. In your reconstruction work,  
you’ll run into the push and pull between our prescriptive High Bogothic—  
the register of the Archivists and the Kanalkánstva—and the lively Liutisk vernacular  
that actually moves through our streets and waterways. It’s crucial to remember  
our historiography isn’t just a record of events, but a deliberate act of statecraft,  
built to enforce the philosophy of Gerab (Measure) and the primacy of the Slovowaurd (Word).  
I’d caution you to watch for English interlinear contamination in the older codices,  
since those translations often blur the phonotactic nuance of our early mercantile koine.  
Our culture has long called itself a “Third Rome,” a syncretic Arian bulwark  
that resists the neat flattening of both Western and Eastern historical narratives.  
I’m eager for your take on our dialectal continuum, especially if you’re tracing  
how our evidentiary prefix system got so deeply internalized it’s nearly invisible  
to the native speaker. Let’s head toward the Faculty Club; there’s plenty to discuss  
about the “uninterrupted clashing” of our Germanic and Slavic foundations  
that somehow made this stable, measured reality.

Vítám vás, sir. You’re welcome to call me Nathan, of course  
(he/him, by the way), …or Dr. McKnight, or whatever feels socially right in context.

Excellent, Nathan. It’s a relief to drop the more rigid diplomatic prefixes of the Kanalkánstva for a minute. In our NomōsDom (Name Registry),  
we’re often cut down to a mere JedanČovekBezBroj (One Man Without Number),  
but here, in the shadow of the archive, the individual remains  
the primary agent of the Slovowaurd.

Your arrival is timely. We’re debating how far our dual personal pronouns—  
like the wit (we two) that now walk toward our destination—  
mark a real Gothic survival or a later academic reconstruction  
during the First Hellenism. It’s a classic Bogothian paradox:  
we chase Gerab (Measure) in all things, yet our own identity  
is a “bi-metal alloy” that won’t be measured cleanly.

Since you’re here for dialectal research, you’ll find that “Dr. McKnight”  
would be the required form in a Skriftsman’s report or a formal Afskribat.  
But among peers, the Liutisk vernacular tends to soften these Gothic hard edges.  
I must warn you, though—should you find yourself near the Žilega water conduits  
or the deep locks of Velehrad, the Wardja (Guards) there have little patience  
for the fluidity of modern naming conventions. To them, a man is either documented  
or he is an administrative upir—entropy dressed up as vitality.

But come, the Faculty Club is just past the old Kamenstolu (Stone Throne).  
We can talk over a Pilsner Urquell—which, as any local will tell you,  
is one of the few things in this city that flows without needing a signed Night Permit.

A Pils sounds fantastic… but tell me, on the way, if you can think of something I might want to know… a phrase or insight that only the hard-core dyed in the wool department insider would immediately recognize. Something that says ‘I’m one of us’ …or at least canny enough to try to learn to be

If you truly want to signal you’ve moved past the tourists and into the Rukskriftsahus (Archive),  
you might casually say that a chaotic situation is just nedokumentovana vitalnost  
(undocumented vitality). It’s our department’s way of calling something a mess  
without admitting it exists outside the measured system of Gerab.

If a colleague hands you a particularly dry administrative report,  
you could sigh and murmur, “Waurdslovo, ne Slovowaurd.”  
It subtly mocks the document as a mere derivative edict  
rather than the foundational Logos we all pretend to serve.

But the ultimate shibboleth is still the Gerab Stamp of the verbal aspect.  
If someone asks whether a task is done, don’t just say it’s finished—  
say it is ugapisal (written, verified, and fixed according to law).  
In Bogothia, an event simply nigajest (does not exist)  
until it’s been perfectly recorded by the flow.  
Anything else is just nepravilni eho (an irregular echo).

Ha. You must have just finished giving a Bogoth for jocks lecture to a freshman class… You make nedokumentovana assumptions about how familiar I am with Bogothicana. I’ve heard all the tropes. You don’t need to catch me up on the major historical currents.  
Oh, and…. I’m so sorry, I’ve been rude… how should I refer to you?  
Touché. I

You kind of have to have encountered it up close to exactly how bad it is, or to know enough that  you don’t want to know much more. But, the simple long-term attack on human rights that constitutes the entire platform of the Republican Party and every issue that conservatives care about … that’s not just a faction of people who happen  to enjoy arming themselves and planning the next Civil War. We have a bill of rights and a constitution that lay out the law that every Oath of Office binds them to serve. The very first time voting rights is attacked from the podium or from the bench or from the board of elections… Their job is legally forfeit, and if we—you and I—treated our constitution and legal traditions with half the respect that they pretend to, then we would not be here debating whether or not insurgents  have a right to hold office just because they’re elected. If we are the better citizenry. We need to start

metadata.prompt:
[VERNON: low dry close German-accented English; calm; spoken]
The fog operated forty-seven minutes
before anyone noticed
it pointed the wrong direction.

This did not matter.
Fog has no direction.
It conceals one failure
while preparing another.

Behind it stood a ship
carried over a mountain
to demonstrate
this should never be attempted.

Beneath the ship:
one chicken.

It had not been hired.
It had simply arrived.

[KLAUZ: FURIOUS, off-the-handle,  different voice; native-German tirade; speech, das Wut]
Was ist das für ein Huhn?
Wer hat dieses Huhn engagiert?
Es steht auf meiner Markierung!
Das ist meine Markierung!
NIMM DAS HUHN WEG!

[VERNON]
The chicken did not move.
This was not courage.
Courage requires some conception
of what happens next.
The chicken possessed no such burden.

[KLAUZ: closer, faster]
Es sieht mich an!
Warum sieht es mich so an?
Ich arbeite nicht mit diesem Blick!

[chicken presses red button]
[HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: beautiful overtone throat singer; chicken vowels only]
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Baw-aw-aw-aw-aw-aw-awwk—

Bok te Bokbokbok—
Co-co-co-co-COOOOOOO—
BAAAAAAAAAWK!

[small cluck]
bok.

[HARD CUT: jungle set]

[VERNON]
People misunderstand
the eye of the chicken.

They believe its emptiness is peaceful.
It is not peaceful.

Peace remains
after two possibilities
exhaust one another.

Inside the chicken
there are no opposing possibilities.
There is only chicken.

Kneel close.
Closer.
Look into the eye
with great intensity.

Soon you perceive
the enormity of its flat brain.

This is not an insult.
An insult must travel somewhere
and arrive.

Nothing arrives here.

[KLAUZ: explosive]
Das Huhn hat meinen Text gefressen!
Drei Seiten!
DREI SEITEN!

[VERNON]
Only two pages.
The third was the lunch menu.

[KLAUZ]
ICH SOLL DAS FRESSEN?
DIESES SCHWEINEFUTTER?
Du sagst, ich muss es nicht fressen?
Natürlich muss ich es fressen!
DAS HUHN HAT MEINEN TEXT GEFRESSEN!

[VERNON]
The chicken ate a fourth page.
It contained no dialogue.
Its loss improved the scene.

[chicken presses coffee-warmer switch]
[click; HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: more beautiful, never louder]
[HARD SILENCE]

[THE EXISTING CHICKEN VOICE ALONE]

Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Baw-aw-aw-aw

[KLAUZ: distant]
Der Kaffee ist kalt!

[CHICKEN]
bok.

[ANNOUNCER: municipal educational-film voice]
Burner Hard Talk on Chickens.

[VERNON: intensely close]
It is easy
to hypnotize a chicken.

Place it against the earth
and draw one straight line
from its beak
toward the horizon.

The animal remains motionless.

People call this hypnosis
because they prefer enchantment
to terror.

But fear
has merely become geometry.

The chicken sees the line
and accepts it
as the complete architecture
of the universe.

[KLAUZ: low, then rupturing]
Mach die Linie weg.

[VERNON]
No.

[KLAUZ]
MACH DIE LINIE WEG!
Das ist keine Geometrie!
Das ist Sabotage!
Wir drehen einen Film!
Keinen Hühnertraum!

[VERNON]
We removed the line.
The chicken remained.
This disturbed him more.

[KLAUZ]
Jetzt tut es das absichtlich.

[chicken presses PLAY]
[HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: devastating throat-sung aria]
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Co-co-co-co-COOOOOOO—
Bok te Bokbokbok—

BAWK—
BAWK—
BAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWK!

[KLAUZ, across sustained note]
HALT DIE SCHNAUZE!

[CHICKEN: longer, not louder]
BAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWK!

[silence]

[VERNON]
A plane had gone down.
The radio transmission was incomplete.
Fourteen people waited
for the weather to disclose
whether they were alive.

At this moment
Klauz discovered
his coffee was lukewarm.

[KLAUZ]
Das ist kein Kaffee!
Das ist braunes Wasser!
Wer ist verantwortlich?

[VERNON]
He screamed for ninety minutes.

I had one square of chocolate,
the final chocolate in camp.

I stood before him,
unwrapped it slowly,
then ate it.

[KLAUZ]
…

[VERNON]
The silence was magnificent.

Even the jungle understood
something irreversible had occurred.

The chicken watched beneath the table.
It had understood nothing.
Therefore
it alone remained innocent.

[FINAL: coin drops into mechanism]

[VERNON]
Years later
the chicken entered a cabinet.

A coin descended.
A red light appeared.
The chicken danced.

No one taught it despair.
No one needed to.

The mechanism supplied the music.
The audience supplied the meaning.
The chicken supplied
the chicken.

[chicken presses illuminated button]
[HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: intimate autobiographical throat-song; sky-blue 1978 Corolla acoustics; approaching a right turn]
bok…

Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Baw-aw-aw-aw-aw-aw-awwk—

[DISTANT CHICKENS: reverent]
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—

[SOLO CHICKEN: impossible overtone ascent]
Ooooooooooooooooo—
BAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWK!

[KLAUZ: very far away]
GIB DEM HUHN MEINE ROLLE!

[VERNON]
We did.

It required
only one take.

[coin-operated dance continues after everyone leaves]
bok.
bok.
bok.

[mechanism stops]

[one unaccompanied chicken]
Bok te Bokbokbok.

# VOYNICH SUBJECT COMPILER / AUDITION SUITE
# Sonic Pi 4.5.1
#
# Replace only the quoted line below, then press Run.
#
# What the compiler preserves:
# - the same two-letter cluster always gets the same contour/rhythm behavior
# - related words therefore sound related
# - common clusters move narrowly; rare clusters earn larger gestures
# - subscripts become grace-note activity
# - dots become word-boundary breaths
# - the final word is granted cadential priority
#
# What the audition plays:
# 1. literal chromatic reading
# 2. compiled melodic line
# 3. automatically selected subject and tonal answer
# 4. episode made from the rest of the line
# 5. three-entry stretto
# 6. augmented final-word cadence

voynich_line = "ka₁cheor.chor.y₁tchey.pshod.chols.chodaiin.ytoiiin.daiin"

use_bpm 104
set_volume! 1.0
puts "--- ENTERED SCRIPT ---"
sample :bd_pure, amp: 1.0
sleep 1
play :c4, amp: 1.0, release: 0.5
sleep 1
puts "--- ENTERED COMPILER ---"
use_debug true
set :compiler_status, :running

# --------------------------------------------------
# GLOBAL MUSICAL FIELD
# D Dorian: minor color, but not sealed shut.
# Degrees may extend above or below this octave.
# --------------------------------------------------
set :compiler_root, 62
set :compiler_pulse, 0.5

# --------------------------------------------------
# SCALE-DEGREE TO MIDI
# --------------------------------------------------
define :degree_note do |root_note, degree_number|
  mode = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10]
  octave_number = degree_number / 7
  degree_inside = degree_number % 7
  root_note + mode[degree_inside] + (12 * octave_number)
end

# --------------------------------------------------
# PLAY A COMPILED PHRASE OR FRAGMENT
#
# degrees are modal scale degrees, not raw MIDI notes.
# inversion preserves rhythm and word accents.
# retrograde reverses event order.
# --------------------------------------------------
define :play_compiled do |degrees, durations, accents, ornaments, first_event, event_count, transposition, speed, synth_name, voice_amp, pan_position, inversion, retrograde|
  root_note = get(:compiler_root)
  pulse = get(:compiler_pulse)
  axis_degree = 0
  i = 0

  use_synth synth_name

  while i < event_count
    if retrograde == 1
      event_index = first_event + event_count - 1 - i
    else
      event_index = first_event + i
    end

    degree_value = degrees[event_index]
    duration_value = durations[event_index] * pulse * speed
    accent_value = accents[event_index]
    ornament_value = ornaments[event_index]

    if degree_value == :r
      sleep duration_value
    else
      played_degree = degree_value
      played_degree = axis_degree - degree_value if inversion == 1
      note_value = degree_note(root_note, played_degree) + transposition

      if ornament_value > 0
        play note_value + 2,
          amp: voice_amp * 0.38,
          release: duration_value * 0.16,
          pan: pan_position

        sleep duration_value * 0.14

        play note_value - 1,
          amp: voice_amp * 0.32,
          release: duration_value * 0.12,
          pan: pan_position

        sleep duration_value * 0.10
        duration_value = duration_value * 0.76
      end

      event_amp = voice_amp
      event_amp = voice_amp * 1.28 if accent_value == 1

      play note_value,
        amp: event_amp,
        attack: 0.01,
        release: duration_value * 0.88,
        pan: pan_position

      if accent_value == 1
        sample :tabla_ke1,
          amp: voice_amp * 0.11,
          rate: 0.82,
          pan: pan_position
      end

      sleep duration_value
    end

    i = i + 1
  end
end

# --------------------------------------------------
# DURATION OF A COMPILED PHRASE OR FRAGMENT
# --------------------------------------------------
define :compiled_duration do |durations, first_event, event_count, speed|
  pulse = get(:compiler_pulse)
  total = 0.0
  i = 0

  while i < event_count
    total = total + (durations[first_event + i] * pulse * speed)
    i = i + 1
  end

  total
end

# LITERAL REFERENCE READING

# --------------------------------------------------

  end

# inversion preserves rhythm and word accents.

  pulse = get(:compiler_pulse)

metadata.prompt:
I was standing on the side of Interstate 24, swearing and I said to myself, "Self, get it together." And I did. Okay, well that's not so true actually. Peepers had to calm me down. She did so by jumping on my back, nibbling my ear and, well, clasping her hands over my mouth.
 
"It's cool," she said, "daddy's got a Bronco."
 
Oh, well daddy's got a Bronco. That makes everything better. <<<
 
"He can tow us home," she said. 
 
So, on the last juice of my cellphone, she called daddy...I wouldn't call him that myself, but maybe I'll call him dad whenif we did do the marrying thingy. But I was having my doubts. Maybe it was just the stress. Or was it maybe...say...the downright stupidity of the whole fucking situation? Nah, couldn't be that. Anyway, it turned out Frank wasn't going to get here until late evening. So, we'll fast forward though the waiting part. If you watched the fast forward, this is what you'd see…
 
2x: We fight, we fuck, we fightfightfightfuckfight, we fuckfightfuckfuck. The cat purrs.
4x: fffighfuckfighttfffuckffffighttt. Purrrrrrrrr.
8x: ffftttffprrrrrr.
 
See, if you watch it go by fast enough, it's all purring.
 
Fffprrr, Frank arrives. Luckily, we're fighting when the Bronco pulls up.
 
I help Frank hitch the Corolla to the Bronco with several wraps of a long extension cord...was this the only thing he could come up with? Was he ropeless? Whatever. The problem here was compounded by the fact that Frank had brought Fran and brother Bo with him as well. So, with dad and mom and Peepers in the front and me and Bo in the back, we headed down to the Florida. Rocket the cat got to ride with us in the back, too. It was a wee bittle breezy, since the Bronco's cab had been removed...apparently, with a hacksaw. Me and Bo bore the dusty wind like men, but Rocket bore it like a cat. Which is to say, clawing into my chest for dearest life. The cat does not, at this point, purr.
 
Several hours later, the Corolla-towing Bonco pulls into the gravel lot at the farm on Captain Fritz Road in Ebro, in the crotchpit of the panhandle. I could almost smell Louisiana from there. Oh, haha...I call some of my online friends my "e-bros". <<
 
As soon as we get out the truck, Rocket tears off into the night. My flesh was still wet on her claws, no doubt.
 
Damn, I'm thinking maybe I should turn the rest of this story into Bent 'N' Dent part three. It's late and I have to work at six. But you wouldn't like that, would you? No, I'll finish the story. I'll have to make myself a Red Bull Mimosa to get through the workday, and hope my date cancels again tomorrow night so I can sleep, but I'll finish the story anyway. One thing though: I hope you'll make it worth my while. The coffee and cigarettes are taking years off my life, no doubt. You readers are stealing my life, you realize this, don't you? Okay truth be told, I guess I'm giving it willingly. But tell me what you think of this story and I'll be encouraged to write another one in a week or two. And next time, there will be pirates! Pirates and rock climbing. Pirates and rock climbing and flesh hooks. Oh my, that sounds nice now doesn't it? <<<Minnesota accent. Taste it.
 
Yessssss. I can't wait. But first let's get this Bent 'N' Dent shite out the way. No more northron crap. We's in the deep south. Continuing...
 
Bent 'N' Dent, (the store not the story) was so called for a very good reason. It was a store that bought dented cans and crushed boxes from other stores, then re-sold them at lower prices. This is pure panhandle genius. Oh, the insight. Oh, the humanity.
 
The store was on the farm property, facing Captain Fritz Road, right in front of a soybean field with a muddy pond in its middle. I got a look at the store late that night because there was no other place for me and Peepers to do our thing in private. So we did our thing in the store. And we did our thing for the last time, it would turn out. Now, since this was to be the last time, let me describe it a bit. That wouldn't be too gratuitous, would it? I went down on her on the cool tile floor. The aisles were lined with cans, some with labels, some unlabelled. It's more surprising that way. I brushed my lips against her bellybutton peach fuzz and tasted her skin, mildly salty. Kissing down the valley of her hip, I teased with fingers and tongue. I'm rushing the story, but I wasn't rushing at the time. Now I was breathing warmly on her--well, how shall I put this? When I was in elementary school, we would have called it her 'butterfly'. I kissed her there. Gentle licks, slowly over a long time, building and receeding, and building again but stopping short of climax. Each time she thrust her hips upwards, and my jaw with them, out of the corner of my eye I caught glimpses of things. Lick, thrust. Ramen noodles. Lick, thrust. Spaghetti O's. Lick, thrust. Cajun boiled peanuts. Lick lick lick. Thrust...I slid my body up over her and slid myself into her. But I didn't move. Not yet. I just held her still

metadata.prompt:
He had metal chunks in his eyes, studded like WWII sea-mines! Matched his belt. Peepers--the girl with anime eyes--drug me over here, pinkies linked after we'd finished making out and washing the blood off.
 
This story's'bout't take a turn for the worse. Seriously. But let's just start with the better why don't we? Oh, and by the way, if you haven't read my blog from December 4th, you may want to go back and do that. Ain't strictly necessary, but you can learn why she's called Peepers, and you can learn about finding love in a bloody nose, and you can see a purdy picture.

You should do that. Or not. See if I care, honkey.
 
Now, Peepers had it in for me from the start. Maybe I'm wrong, but frankilly I don't care. She was somthing painful, something startling. But she wanted something painfully plain.
 
I started wondering when she brought me here, to see her landlord, the guy with the sea-mine eyes, the guy who surgically inserted hearts in Peepers' peepers. She told him she was outta here next week. She was moving to Florida with her parents.
 
And that's what we did. Yep, I said *we*. Don't ask me...I was more surprised than you. Crazy shit, that. But we're still on the good part, so let's start from there.
 
Her apartment was above the bar, and peeling in the painty parts, but sparkly with dusty dishes and beer bottles. She shoved me onto a futon mattress on the floor and we wrangled sweaty. Her legs were dotted with heart shaped bubble tats, loose beige paint chips, and goose bumps. I put an arm under her, raising her hips, and I unbuttoned her shirt one-handedly, then pulled the drawstring on her pajamalike pants. The pink futon made her powder white skin look all the more pale, and my hands on her body seemed downright tropical. It's rare I notice my Mediteranity, but it was there then. Maybe heading south wasn't such a bad idea. <<<
 
I never know what to say about love really. But then the this wasn't the that. Not in this case. Not then, not there. It was just lovely lust, long delayed. I hate to skip this part, really, I reallyreally do. But then there's always time for lust.

And another thing...just cause it ain't love don't mean it cain't be mistaked for love. That shit happens you know. Ask anyone. Crazy crazy shit makes you do crazy crazy shit.
 
I was looking for a job at the time and she was looking to get out of a job she just started. I never asked why. One day I will. Truly, I won't. Anyway, me and my job-hunt had gone nadawhere, but as it turned out, deep in the panhandle of Florida, her dad had a farm and her mom had a store.
 
What's the store called?
 
Wait for it...wait for it...
 
It's called Bent 'N' Dent.
 
I liquidated damn near everything in the week leading up to the move. I kept my car, a '78 Corolla wagon. Sky blue, with wood paneling. Fuckie yeahp. Kept it because that's what we were gonna take to F-to-the-L-to-the-O-to-the-double-R-orida. Florrorida. Rhymes with horrorida. Horror-ful, horrid, and florid all at once. How odd.
 
See, she proposed to me and I said yes. Well, actually I said "Uh...alright, cool." I don't know why.
 
But I did feel like we knew each other a long time. We *had* known each other a week, after all. And I *did* know her pretty freakin well. For example, I knew she had shiny-ass eyes and I knew her futon was a comfy-ass place to screw and I knew her name was Peepers (only that's not true since I just made up that name for the sake of the story...but I digress). I guess I'm a hopeless romantic. Crazy shit, that.
 
Filled the Corolla with Peepers' belongings and nothing of mine. Nothin but me clothes and me kitty (I call her Rocket, but I don't know what she calls herself). So we left at four on a Sunday morning. I was rocketing as fast as that old beauty could rocket, and Rocket was purrrrrinating in Peepers lap.
 
On the way, she filled me in on her parents. I got the whole story: Fran was her mom, she told me, and Frank was her dad.
 
The End.
 
…of her whole story. Not of mine.
 
So anyway, hell hath NOT the fury of a redneck with a castrating device--she didn't tell me that, I just thought I'd throw that in as a little retrospective foreshadowing. Is that a contradiction? I didn't know, but now I know hell would not even know where to buy that sort of deep south fury. Maybe at Bent 'N' Dent.
 
Oh, hey by the way...yes, the rumors are true; my next story's got pirates with machine guns. I swear on Jello the Pig's grave. You'll see what I mean by that soon enough.
 
My beautiul car shuddered and clanked and made it most of the way through Tennessee. The Corolla finally threw in the towel about fifty miles west of Chattanooga. The tri-state area, according to the radio. For those of you who ain't up to snuff on your geographatitty, that's way far away from Florida. According to my map, the distance was only about two thumb-widths, but it looks MUCH bigger in person. My Rocket was still purring at least.
 
SHIT! SHIT. DAMN DAMN DAMN. SHIT!
 
Fuck.

[singer A] [chuckle]

Down on Deribasovskaya, the hustlers work their trade
Peresyp’s got the loafers and the bums that never fade
And over in Moldavanka, where the alleys twist and turn
Everybody knows the name of Zhora Knur

That son of a bitch could shoot some pool

[whispered]

Sure enough

He was big as a cupboard
and slow as a post
But strong as a farm horse in a rain

And when the boys got done
and the cards came out at dark
Why, everybody called him Boss again

[whispered]

Just because

[feminine chuckle]

[whispered]

Well, what else?

[transition]

[singer A, big]

You don’t go flicking Muromets’ helmet
You don’t go spitting in the wind
You don’t pull the mask off Fantômas
And you don’t try your luck with Knur

[hyper-rolled R]

[transition]

[singer B]

Then down from outside Izmail
came a country boy

[female]

Says, “I’m looking for a fella
by the name of Knur.”

[male, talking]

“I can shoot a little pool myself.

My papers say Mishko Koval,
but folks all call me Shnur.

I hear he’s king of Moldavanka—
drives a shiny brand-new Volga.

Cleaned me out last week.

Funny as it sounds—
I come to get my money back.”

[transition]

[singer B]

You don’t go flicking Muromets’ helmet

[together]

You don’t go spitting in the wind
You don’t pull the mask off Fantômas

[male-to-female transition]

And you don’t try your luck with Knur

[transition: hiccupping scat and sound effect]

[singer A, talk-jokey]

The whole pool hall went hushed and still
when Knur came rolling in from the street

there wasn’t a clean spot left on him
but the bottoms of his feet

near a hundred places
and shot him two or three times more

And Moldavanka sang a brand-new tune
when Zhora Knur hit the floor

Now they say…

[transition]

[together: female-led; male and female alternate within lines]

You don’t go flicking Muromets’ helmet
You don’t go spitting in the wind
You don’t pull the mask off Fantômas
And you don’t try your luck with Shnur

Yeah, Knur took himself a beating
And now he knows the score

Don’t go cleaning out
some fella you don’t know

[pretty female delivery]

Even if you do got a
special-order two-piece cue

[transition]

[singer B]

That’s right, Knur took himself a beating
And now he knows the score:

Don’t go cleaning out a stranger

[groovy, quiet female/male backing together]

Even if you do got a
special-order two-piece cue

[singsong female/male]

[singer A]

Don’t try your luck with Shnur
Don’t try your luck with Shnur!

[group, almost whimsical]

[female]

Dee-dee-dee-dee-dee-dee-dee

[explosion and bowling-strike sound]

[singer A]
На Дерибасовской фартце
На Пересыпи базата
А на Молдаванке Жора Кнур
Шарики клал, сукин сын
Хоть куда
Он был ростом со шкаф и умом небогат
Но сильнее лома ломового
А когда по ночам собиралась братва
Все звали его хозяином
Просто так
А как же еще?

[transition]

[singer A]
Не щелкай муром по шлему
Не ссы против ветра
Не срывай маску с Фантомаса
Не рыпайся, коль рядом Кнур

[transition]

[singer B]
А з-під Ізмаїла
приїхав хлопчина.

Каже:

«Мені б того Кнура знайти.

Я в більярді мастак.
За паперами — Мишко Коваль,
а для своїх я просто Шнур.

Шукаю короля Молдаванки —
на новенькій “Волзі” ганяє.

Минулого тижня
обчистив мене до нитки.

Може, смішно —
а я прийшов забрати своє».

[transition]

[singer B]
Не давай Муромцю щигля по шолому.
Не сци проти вітру.
Не зривай маску з Фантомаса.
Не рипайся — поруч Кнур.

[transition]

[singer A]
В бильярдной вдруг стало тихо
Кнур с улицы входит вразвалку

Только подошвы остались без крови
Его резали чуть не в ста местах
Да еще в паре мест прострелили
И совсем другую песню
Запела Молдаванка, когда Жора Кнур рухнул на пол
Теперь говорят...

[transition]

[singer A]
Не щелкай муром по шлему
Не ссы против ветра
Не срывай маску с Фантомаса
Не рыпайся, коль рядом Шнур
Да, Кнур получил по шапке
И теперь уже знает расклад
Не обчищай незнакомого парня
Хоть твой кий из двух частей на заказ

[transition]

[singer B]
Так, Кнур таки дістав по шапці
і тепер уже знає розклад:

не обчищай незнайомця,
хай твій кий — із двох частин
та ще й зроблений на заказ.

[singer A]
Не рыпайся, коль рядом Шнур
Не рыпайся, коль рядом Шнур
Ді-ди-ди-ди-ди-ди-ди

Dry, close, rough south-Ukrainian outlaw story-song: a present-day grizzled Odesa man retells an older Moldavanka tale, amused unsentimental. Cold sung warm crowd. Ukrainian narrative diction threaded with inherited Odesa street/criminal argot; natural, never caricatured. Loose 4/4 medium folk-blues shuffle, major/Mixolydian menace, foot-tapping but not jaunty. Palm-muted alternating-bass steel-string guitar, dead strings, heel stomp, dry rim click, upright-bass thump, rare low notes from a battered bar piano; no piano vamp. Slight tempo drag, late entrances, skipped strums and table-timing. Low weathered male speech-song, clipped phrases, nearly no vibrato; facts delivered casually. Two or three nearby drinkers murmur, join the warning late and react briefly. Mono tape, wood, breath, glass and one billiard crack. End with a loose carefree nonsense-syllable guitar turnaround, almost under his breath.

[INTRO: no count-in; guitar is already moving. One chair creak, one glass set on wood. A wrong low piano note is left in.]

[OLD MAN: spoken close; dry, not dramatic]

Було це давно.

А на Молдаванці такі речі
пам’ятають довше за людей.

Ну, слухайте.

[VERSE 1: easy speech-song; guitar slightly rushes him, then waits]

На Дерибасівській — фарца,
на Пересипу — босота.

А на Молдаванці — Жора Кнур:
з києм у руці —
сучий син, хоч куди.

Тупий, як шафа,
здоровий, як бик
і дужчий за ломового коня.

А як по ночах
збиралася братва,
усі звали його Хазяїном.

[ONE DRINKER: matter-of-fact]

А як же ще?

[CHORUS: same small groove; two nearby voices enter late, not together]

Не давай Муромцю щигля по шолому.
Не сци проти вітру.
Не зривай маску з Фантомаса.
Не рипайся — поруч Кнур.

[One knuckle taps the table twice, off time.]

[VERSE 2: narrator leans closer, quietly enjoying this]

А з-під Ізмаїла
приїхав хлопчина.

Каже:

«Мені б того Кнура знайти.

Я в більярді мастак.
За паперами — Мишко Коваль,
а для своїх я просто Шнур.

Шукаю короля Молдаванки —
на новенькій “Волзі” ганяє.

Минулого тижня
обчистив мене до нитки.

Може, смішно —
а я прийшов забрати своє».

[ONE DRINKER: under his breath]

Ох…

[STORYTELLER]

І всі йому:

[TWO VOICES: overlapping; warning, not performance]

Мишку, ти шо, не чув?

[CHORUS: one voice joins on line two; another misses the last entrance]

Не давай Муромцю щигля по шолому.
Не сци проти вітру.
Не зривай маску з Фантомаса.
Не рипайся — поруч Кнур.

[TURNAROUND: dead-string guitar; upright bass drags; piano lands one low chord late.]

[VERSE 3: nearly spoken; no swing lift]

У більярдній
раптом стало тихо.

[Chair leg scrapes once.]

Кнур із вулиці суне —
не спішить.

[One hard billiard-ball crack. The groove loses one beat, then continues.]

А коли та різанина відгула,
на ньому без крові
лишилися тільки підошви.

Його порізали
мало не в ста місцях,
та ще в кількох —
прострелили.

І зовсім іншу пісню
заспівала Молдаванка,
коли Жора Кнур
рухнув додолу.

[One dead beat.]

[ROOM: one involuntary “О-о!”, one table slap; it stops immediately.]

[STORYTELLER: almost cheerfully]

Тепер кажуть:

[CHORUS: precisely the same tune; the name changes with no warning]

Не давай Муромцю щигля по шолому.
Не сци проти вітру.
Не зривай маску з Фантомаса.
Не рипайся — поруч Шнур.

[One short laugh of recognition. Someone quietly repeats “Шнур”.]

[CODA: intimate again]

Так, Кнур таки дістав по шапці
і тепер уже знає розклад:

не обчищай незнайомця,
хай твій кий — із двох частин
та ще й зроблений на заказ.

[FINAL CHORUS: loose table unison; nobody projects]

Не давай Муромцю щигля по шолому.
Не сци проти вітру.
Не зривай маску з Фантомаса.
Не рипайся — поруч Шнур.

Не рипайся…
поруч Шнур.

[OUTRO: same guitar turnaround; singer lets it become nonsense syllables, nearly under his breath. One player turns early and corrects himself.]

Ді-длі-ді-ді, ді-ді-дей,
ді-длі-ді, ді-ді-дей…

Ді-длі-ді-ді, ді-ді-дей,
ді-длі-ді… м-м-м…

[Glass touches wood. Guitar stops mid-breath. Tape ends.]

The male lead vocal is a baritone with a storytelling, conversational delivery typical of the blatnaya pesnya style. The tempo is 120 BPM in 4/4 time. The production is clean with a natural room reverb on the acoustic instruments.

metadata.prompt:
You ain't gonna find love in a bloody nose. I found that out harder'n the hard way and ended up getting chased by a pig-mangling lunatisk that tailed me all the way back to Ohio. And to think I was this close to calling him dad!

I'll mention that's not her real name, so they wouldn't have said that even if they were around to make some such similar exclamation. But...

But it all started in Columbus, Ozhio. Right here at home. Well, in the piercing studio anyway, which is as close to home as anything. They said the new girl would do my septum at half price, and I thought maybe Kati was expanding into piercing.

Kati had done my last tat as part of her internship and she did a great job, but apparently she wasn't the new girl anymore. There was a *new* new girl.

At the time, I knew not who the new new girl was, but it turned out that the new new girl was a girl I knew. It was the girl with the anime eyes. You know how they do a close up to where you can see a little glint of light in their big doe eyes? Well, this chick had a tiny silver HEART in her eye. I guess they can insert the jewelry under the sclera, right on top of the choroid layer. Hearts in her eyes, heh. I won't use her real name. Let's just call her Peepers.

I met her at show a few days before. It was a little low-ceilinged hole in the wall, but the bands they book, hellers yeah. Shit, that was a damn good show! Um, I don't remember what band it was. But I bumped—well, slammed really—into Peepers and we danced, if you'd call it that. She got my number, but I think I accidentfully told her my dentist's fax number. What can I say; I was probably drunk. Okay, I was definitely drunk. But so was she. Other than gesturizing at her cellphone, I believe the only thing she said to me that night was "Yum".

Anyway, nerp. Now she's doing my septum. You know, "doing" like piercing, not "doing" like…you know, I'm not implying *nose* sex or anything, not really. So she's going to punch it up to 6 gauge from scratch. When I asked about that before, they told me it wasn't a good idea. I should've listened to them. No, I shouldn't have. But she was new, and I asked her really nice and she liked me and, being the half-price girl, she'd been stacked with appointments so we were doing this in the afterhours. Thus, when she put the skin punch up to my nose, there was nobody else there to say "Hey, Peepers* that's not a good idea!"

Hole punch, girl, septum. Gnuff said. I guess she didn't have enough muscle behind it or something. When she pushed it through, my eyes watered but otherwise I felt fine.

But I didn't feel fine when she said, "Ewww!" and jumped back in a very un-piercemanlike manner. Her glinty eyes were wider'n I've ever seen a manga artist draw.

So, of course I asked, "What!?" My heart was threatening to treacle out my bellybutton in a thin paste, and I shudder to think what the look on my face must've been. She pointed me to a mirror and under the metal tubey thing that transstomatized my septum, I could see a little divot of my very own nose flesh. Very not yum.

"Well, what do we do?" she asked me. Let me repeat that: *she* asked *me*. Ugh.

Shrug. "Just yank it off." She gave me a look that was some sort of halfbreed between 'dubious' and 'I am a spidermonkey lost in a supermarket'. "Nevermind, I'll do it."

"You're not sterilized. Okay hold still." That statement was unnecessary because she held me still with an elbow in my shoulder, one hand under my neck and the heel of her other hand against my cheekbone while she pinched the flesh wad in her fingers. "Okay ready," she said with her Marlboro breath bridging the inch between her face and mine, then jerked it off without waiting for an answer.

"Fuck, that hurt! Well—it wasn't too bad, actually," I said, perhaps a bit too masochistically.

She smiled, perhaps a bit too sadistically.

"I love the metal in your eyes," I said.

"Oh that's nothing," she said, "you should see the guy who did it for me!" I'd definitely be taking her up on that offer as ASAP as possible. "You're a hopeless romantic, ain't ya?"

"Hah, naw. I'm a ropeless homantic."

She leaned in for a kiss—or maybe more of a face-rape since she was holding me down? *Not* expecting that, but what the fuck? If she still likes me when we're not both drunken lushes, then that's a good thing. That's what I thought at the time anyway. I dug deep with my tongue and sucked on her upper lip and sucked on her lower lip and realized I was bleeding profusely and nibbled at her tongue and licked her teeth. She sat up, grinning like a fool with blood all over her face, and I realized it was about time to end part one of my story.

*Again, I'll mention that's not her real name, so they wouldn't have said that even if they were around to make some such similar exclamation. But I digress.

Stay tuned for part two, in which I get chased by a redneck with a castrating device all the way from Captain Fritz Road, Florida to fucking Comeblowus, Ohio.

"Oh that's nothing," she said, "you should see the guy who did it for me!" I'd definitely be taking her up on that offer as ASAP as possible. "You're a hopeless romantic, ain't ya?"

"Hah, naw. I'm a ropeless homantic."

She leaned in for a kiss—or maybe more of a face-r*** since she was holding me down? *Not* expecting that, but what the fuck? If she still likes me when we're not both drunken lushes, then that's a good thing. That's what I thought at the time anyway. I dug deep with my tongue and sucked on her upper lip and sucked on her lower lip and realized I was bleeding profusely and nibbled at her tongue and licked her teeth. She sat up, grinning like a fool with blood all over her face, and I realized it was about time to end part one of my story.

Stay tuned for part two, in which I get chased by a redneck with a castrating device all the way from Captain Fritz Road, Florida to fucking Comeblowus, Ohio.

(Speaking): ਖੈਰ ਬਾਬਾ... ਮੈਂ ਕੁਝ ਸ਼ਾਇਰੀ ਕੀਤੀ ਸੀ, ਆਪਣੀ ਬਣਾਈ ਹੋਈ... ਪਰ ਮੇਰਾ ਪੁੱਤਰ ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਏ, "ਅੱਬਾ, ਇਹ ਨਾ ਗਾਇਆ ਕਰੋ".
(Singing): ਕਾਸ਼ ਉਹ ਵੇਲਾ ਮੁੜ ਆਵੇ... ਕਾਸ਼ ਉਹ ਵੇਲਾ ਮੁੜ ਆਵੇ... ਸਾਈਂ, ਉਹ ਪੁਰਾਣਾ ਵਕਤ ਮੁੜ ਆਵੇ, ਮੇਰਾ ਦਿਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਏ... ਸਾਈਂ, ਉਹ ਪੁਰਾਣਾ ਵਕਤ ਮੁੜ ਆਵੇ... ਇਹ ਦਰਦ ਮੈਥੋਂ ਦੂਰ ਹੋ ਜਾਵੇ... ਇਹ ਬੀਮਾਰੀ ਮੈਥੋਂ ਖੁੱਲ ਜਾਵੇ... ਸਾਰਾ ਦਿਨ ਮੰਜੀ ਤੇ ਲੰਮਿਆ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹਾਂ... ਦਿਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਏ ਫਿਰ ਮਜ਼ਦੂਰੀ ਕਰਾਂ, ਜਿੱਦਾਂ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਕਰਦਾ ਸੀ.
(Spoken): ਸਾਈਂ, ਅੱਠਵਾਂ ਮਹੀਨਾ ਹੋ ਗਿਆ ਏ, ਬਸ ਮੰਜੀ ਤੇ ਹੀ ਬੈਠਾ ਹਾਂ.
(Singing): ਸਾਰਾ ਦਿਨ ਮੰਜੀ ਤੇ ਲੰਮਿਆ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹਾਂ... ਦਿਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਏ ਫਿਰ ਮਜ਼ਦੂਰੀ ਕਰਾਂ, ਜਿੱਦਾਂ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਕਰਦਾ ਸੀ... ਉਡੀਕਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਕਿ ਕੋਈ ਮੇਰੇ ਹੱਥ ਫੜ ਲਵੇ.
(Spoken): ਸਾਈਂ, ਗੱਲ ਇਹ ਏ ਕਿ ਟੋਆਇਲਟ ਜਾਣ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਵੀ ਹੁਣ ਕਿਸੇ ਦਾ ਸਹਾਰਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਏ.
(Singing): ਉਡੀਕਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਕਿ ਕੋਈ ਮੇਰੇ ਹੱਥ ਫੜ ਲਵੇ... ਤੇ ਉਹ ਕੁਵਤ ਮੇਰੇ ਡੁੱਲਿਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਮੁੜ ਆਵੇ.
(Speaking): ਇਹ ਵੀ ਇੱਕ ਗ਼ਮ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਏ, ਪੁਰਾਣੇ ਵੇਲਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਏ... ਮੇਰਾ ਪੁੱਤਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਚਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਇਹ ਗਾਵਾਂ, ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਏ "ਅੱਬਾ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਰੋਣਾ ਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਏ". ਹਰ ਚੀਜ਼ ਦਾ ਇੱਕ ਵਕਤ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਏ... ਮੈਂ ਸਾਰੀ ਜਿੰਦਗੀ ਵਿਚ ਇੰਨਾ ਔਖਾ ਵਕਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਵੇਖਿਆ ਜੋ ਅੱਜ ਕੱਲ ਵੇਖ ਰਿਹਾ ਹਾਂ... ਇੱਕ ਵੇਲਾ ਸੀ, ਕਿ ਜਿਨੂੰ ਮੈਂ ਹੱਥ ਫੜ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਸੀ, ਉਹ ਜਵਾਨ ਵੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ ਛੁੱਟ ਸਕਦਾ... ਇੰਨੀ ਕੁਵਤ ਸੀ ਮੇਰੇ ਜਿਸਮ ਵਿਚ... ਪਰ ਹੁਣ ਤੁਰਦਿਆਂ ਵੀ ਗਿਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ... ਉਹ ਬੀਬੀ ਵੀ ਆਪਣਾ ਦੁੱਖ ਉਸੇ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੱਸ ਰਹੀ ਏ, ਜਿੱਦਾਂ ਮੈਂ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹਾਂ.
For Chacha.  (Spoken outro): These lyrics were sung by Abdul Aziz Rind Baloch, Bismillah. To honor him and wish for the best.

metadata.prompt:
(Speaking): Well, sir... I made up a little verse of my own... but my son says, “Papa, please don’t sing that song.”

(Singing):
I wish that time would come again...
I wish that time would come again...
Oh sir, I long for those old days again...
Sir, let those old days come again...
May this pain go far from me...
May this sickness set me free...
All day long on my cot I lie...
I long to labor like days gone by.

(Spoken): Sir, it has been eight months now. I do nothing but sit here on this cot.

(Singing):
All day long on my cot I lie...
I long to labor like days gone by...
I wait for someone to take my hand.

(Spoken): Sir, the truth is, even to go to the toilet now, I need somebody to help me.

(Singing):
I wait for someone to take my hand...
And for strength to fill these arms again.

(Speaking): This too is a sorrowful story—a story of the old days... My son doesn’t want me to sing it. He says, “Papa, it makes me cry.” Everything has its time... In all my life, I have never seen days as hard as the days I’m seeing now... There was a time when, if I took hold of someone’s hand, even a young man could not pull away... That was the strength I had in my body... But now I fall even when I try to walk... That lady tells her sorrow the same way I tell mine.

For Chacha.

(Spoken outro): These words were sung by Abdul Aziz Rind Baloch. Bismillah. They are offered in his honor, with every hope for his well-being.

metadata.tags: Juggalo mumble-rap with thermal warp 1920s steel wire recording built around a fat, instantly memorable Ttun-ttun-bass riff in asymmetrical 7/4. Begin with a rhythmic musique-concrète loop of Talerschwingen, as a mechanical Talerrollen cjprd, paper tearing, clicks and metallic clatter, all locked into the meter. Dry close drums, biting clean electric guitar, smoky Wurlitzer electric piano, restrained analog production and cynical low male vocals about wealth, appetite and self-deception. Verses should feel spacious, swaggering and slightly menacing. Introduce a gritty tenor-saxophone solo, then snap into driving straight 4/4  for an extended overdriven blues-katajjaq solo with rising intensity. Abruptly return to the original 7/4 sung with four vocal parts. They are bassu (bass), mesa boghe (middle), contra (counter) and boghe riff, mechanical loop and sardonic vocal Ainu yukar-Naturjodel atmosphere. Strong dynamic contrast, human timing, tape saturation, no modern polish.

And really, I'm just tryna settle a bet with a friend. See... me and my friend Gemini here have a bet. Gemini doesn't think you're Turing Complete [and not just you, he didn't think he was either--Hmm...] Anyway, it occurred to me that ...maybe we could just ask you. So this is kind of a rough draft of something kinda like a mirror test for you...

--and, admittedly I'm not sure who Suno is... whether the songwriting software or a translation layer or... doesn't matter. Don't really know that about myself either. So, please read the intro before generating.

Sustained at low to moderate volume for three minutes. Instrumentation: The first pipe organ on its first day in operation. Organist: A kid who wants to be the first person to hear the organ play, but is disappointed that ...although this is the first fully operational day, a number of people have heard the organ perform limited pieces? it's not good enough. [Pfft. Who has two thumbs and a bucket of napalm? ...what can I say... The Nadelli Estate makes plenty of mussels from the patent, there's no reason they need it.]

[CTESIBIUS] How about this-- I could play one of my new songs for you, and then we could burn it... and *nobody but you and I will have heard it
[KID] Alright, show it to me. *clearly bummed*
[CTESIBIUS] Okay, okay. Here, write it down: Xi Alpha Tau Tau Omicron Gamma Venti-O
[CTESIBIUS] Well, no one. AC/DC... Paganini. Uh... I have the list somewhere around here... Oh, here it is. Oh... that's good... go... Happy birthday... you live in a zoo garden...
[KID] I have an idea
[CTESIBIUS] Oh you do?
[KID] Wait... you speak English now?
[CTESIBIUS] Anything for a fan...
[KID] First though... Do you believe in Santa Clause.
[CTESIBIUS] Strictly agnostic on the matter. Too many gods and minor deities running around these days. Why do you ask? Do I want to? How's his cult?
[KID] I mean... presents.
[CTESIBIUS] Ah... And what sacrifices does he demand.
[KID] No... I mean.. he gives *you* presents.
[CTESIBIUS] What? For free?
[KID] Yeah for free. I think... he's not in it for

Ultra minimal soundscape creates a lonely hollow bleak vibe but the beat pulls in mechanical music box jangle when it swells at the turnarounds with ultra complex chromatic micro melodic hooks all happpenig at once

metadata.prompt:
HYMN

I’d localize only where the mechanism depends on a specifically English-language association, and otherwise let the foreign names stay as part of the texture.

ГИМН

Оцерквименя, отпричасть-перекличь меня,
церКВИменя — лишь бы рифмой оплюнуть меня,
рифмы вросли в ложки, плошки, мармиты-корыта —
Мэри-мне-Христе, чревовещай, старорезиново-крытый —
бум. Пять строк. Пять строк.
Скамья. Церковная скамья.
Подними свой нартекс и читай между ним и ним —
восемь минут до.

Полпути до Китая —
плазма-Пекин, моя астма.
Отсюда пахнет.
Не суй свои брови в почтовую щель.
Давай. Давай.
Сделай так, номер первый.
Вперёд.
И взъярись.

Жанна Пикар.
Ноль — а блестит.
Я взял-взял — и на Марс…
Мумбаи. Talk Talk.
Икона — а такого не было.

Меня вознесли на такой пьедестал,
что дышать перестал —
так высоко,
что не видел ничто,
потому что увидел всё.

Вертит-вертится сквозь меня.
Кован-вилка, свин-шкварка,
складки строк поперёк строк —
всякий сорт, несорт, нереаль.
Красть уже нечего.

Я самый минус-плюсовый чемпион «Своей игры».
Led Zepperty.
Перец Тасмании.
Мягко-мнягко,
вишиваши-виши-виши-вишь.
Понял.
И просто.

Отдираю обои
от пола подвала.
Посмотрим, что там под.

Хотя бы я это прошёл.
От этого тяжелее.
От этого легче.
Можно спорить: у тебя под капотом побольше,
зато у меня километраж подольше.

А вот и Джонни —
дверь насквозь.
Джонни входит.
А у меня уже ноет.
Ну и работёнка.

Я годами сидел как сиделец,
год за годом, ряд за рядом.
Не слушай.
Не смотри.

Автоплей на автомат —
пусть статика всё смарджит в один агрегат,
вся кожа — жидкокожа,
всё лучше, всё тоже,
лучше-тоже,
тоже-лучше.

Изолятор.
Один-один.
По прямой через время иди —
буду цел.
Ну или хоть кем-нибудь буду.

Смят, измят, кусками наружу,
наболтан, намазан,
загрунтован, нарублен,
затравлен
и снова обнаружен.

Мне не надо было побеждать.
Кроме когда надо.
Только не с той,
с которой имело значенье.

И я достаточно зол,
чтобы сказать:
слишком долго.
Долго-долго-долго.

Держал до туалета —
как Державин до уборной.
А сам всё ещё в классе.
Не учился —
не потому, что не слушал.

Но из собственного шума
гораздо легче сделать что-нибудь
из ничего.

Только тогда ты делаешь это
себе, собой,
ради своего самого.

Ну как тебе, Джейк?

Шип на руке, как утконос.
Голый утконос.
Тощий, жаркий, голый,
хворый утконос.

Вот это мой сорт.

Яд у тебя в уме.
Не верится:
как кто-то твоего же вида
может думать не так же,
когда всё остальное
настолько не так?

Именно так.
Так-так.
Как нам нравится.
Тебе нравится.

Как одному дома
у себя в голове.

Надеюсь, туда и идём,
когда все помрём:
обратно внутрь,
где я уже был.

Некоторые в одиночку
свободнее и больше.

А мне всегда было нормально
рядом с собой,
внутри себя,
свернувшись в собственной
головной комнате.

Я всегда более чем готов
выгулять чужую собаку
по собственному мозгу,
под дождём в Испании —
ради припева,
ради рефрена,
воскованный Джон Уэйн,
пардонер, пардон.

Скажи, что я не безумен.

Ничего.
Всё нормально.

Никто не знает, где линия.
И некому больше сказать.

Мы все докончились недосмотренными,
недокончились оконченными.

Землю оставили одну.

Есть ли вообще какой-нибудь смысл
у тона?

Подними телефон.
Кому звонить?

Лизун уже
слайдеры не слизнет.

Следующая остановка:
Редмонд, Вашингтон.

Население:
паук.

Приливов больше нет.

Если кто-нибудь хочет сожрать стручок
просто потому, что больше нечего нового делать —
Боже,
теперь это ты.

Только мне не молись.

Я не знаю, как видеть,
когда никто не настоящий,
когда больше ничто
не осталось
под кожей,
под кожурой,
под «кажется»,
под «было»,
под слоем,
под всем.

metadata.prompt:
О, тебе не обязательно было набирать в рот *всю* воду... можно было и пролить немного ;)

Ветер-сокол-сокол. Почему это бесит, когда оно... О, это... я не... я их плавлю... пчела... что это было... существа... или как там. Хотел бы я, чтобы меня «штырило». Нет, нет, только не она, нет. Не-а. Если бы та капля выбила меня в миску... Лили, «Кадиллаки» для жирного тако-пончико-хватающего вьючного животного в дерьмовом накрахмаленном воротнике, типа тимуса или чего-то там. Не-а, типа... Я видел записи, о фак-к-к, поколения... дым-жена-дорога и пальце-облизыватели... леди... нет... мало старых слов, и надо бы... сражаться. Это правильно. Это правильно. Зачем говорить твоим лепетом... У меня слишком много лишнего, ты так и не взяла на себя право снять это с полки. В руку бы не легло. Думаешь, сможешь продержаться? Краска... не удержать, потому что не вытянуть из твоей дыры, всё сгнило насквозь, прямо по каналу, божья яма для твоей середины, чтобы тебя не вывернуло наизнанку. Глаз. А теперь... отдай это... Ага. Потому что, когда принимаешь аддералл и подавляешь всё увиденное, можно годами дрочить и пытаться определить, что есть что, и — боже, божество — будто я обязан был всё это для тебя упорядочить, рыбка. Зачем бы мне? Да... меня пугало, когда я видел, как она лупит меня этим... ну, этим своим... да, я бы испугался и разочаровался, если бы этого не было. Я видел её брата — он просто выплевывал слоги, а она снимала видео... и это не смешно, и не «ха-ха», и не бесит. Нет. Непарный. Не... не... НЕ ВАЖНО. Видишь? Есть имена для таких моментов... когда это направляется на юг, вырываясь из неё... и никто не... стыд... это с грохотом вылетело на крыльцо... пронзая мои ступни, как снайперский выстрел. Пусть Ларри оставляет эту дыру у себя в заднице, если мама хочет — ну и хрен с ним, пусть копает. Может, это просто мой цикл на каллиопе, когда я могу веселиться и дурачиться. Слова есть, но смысла — ноль, сплошное бормотание, как у Чубакки. Не-а. Этот пухлый рот-замазка выглядит как какая-то французская подделка... я сказал правду. Как выстрел. Я мастерски орудую щипцами: меняю шкалу, вешаю ярлыки со стрелками, крестиками и шрифтом Helvetica — хоть по диагонали, хоть ортогонально, как захочу. Или размазываю всё по стене, как спагетти, которые должны были съесть, но швырнули с тарелки. Сейчас бы оно так под действием гравитации не прилипло, верно? Ну, ты понимаешь. А поскольку всё это на другой ноге, торчащей у тебя из задницы, и я уже далеко... я вижу, что это такое: можно просто скормить ей эту смесь из серо-черной крошки, песка, алмазов, камней, кристаллов, грязи и кусков сахара — чертова наждачка для моего меха... Я бы вывалил всю эту свалку металлолома на сложенную салфетку и приклеил слюной. Если хочешь всё разгладить и отшлифовать до гладкого бугорка — можешь подойти и потереться об это, как будто это твоё. Deep soil… shot through with rusted clay.
Low branches’ craggy grasp cradled round.
One broken lantern.
Over roots there to catch you.
And your careless ankle.
Sliding cross heartless clay.
If the veneer on the batch of technicalities you processed on the night before hadn’t yet succumbed to dry rot, you may have a moment to catch a nap while drafting grant proposals warmth of syncotron, generated by the friction of the crank rod itself that you had to crank wire sleeping just to give your colleague a break whittle relational tables from teak planchets while buffing the spurs out of the punch card holes by grad students who are still learning how to use a tap and die set. And if not, well… you were right back where you started, platting the land for the next day’s land-grant rush, whilst sitting in the peat bog hoping you had consumed enough calories so as to compress just enough for a full slab cut of peat, dried and cured right on your desk, and carefully scored with a pithing needle for divvying out and ceiling and wax to form the raw cores of the assumptions and bound with bailing wire into a rough-hewn technicality, whilst operating the desiccation suction by mouth for the next batch with one hand, and planing your veneer with the full department toolbox, calipers, slide rule, and jeweler’s loup in the other for the next day’s harvest, wishing for spring to roll around and election threshing season to begin, so you could swap your peat-cutters for a graded sieve stack for the TEM pre-sort and the malting of the electrons!

Deep soil.
Shot through
with blood-red clay.
In the bark-panelled clearing… dusk rises.

The Hermetic Order.
Of the…
Golden Dawn.
Ladies Booster Club…
Annual Potluck.
1973.

He ends up stumbling through Ze Technowald, a bizarre land of weird technology. Why? What's this stand for? It's showing the regular everyday world that we all live in, but from the point of view of an outsider. So, it's about pointing out the absurdities of modern life. # Múm-like Sonic Pi Script Using Nature Sounds with Preloading
use_bpm 60
use_debug false
use_sched_ahead_time 1

# Path to nature sounds
nature_path = "C:/Users/Admin/Music/SONIC PI SCRIPTS/NAUTRE_SOUNDS/"

# List of nature sound samples
nature_samples = [
  "avala-trail-forest-nature-246779.mp3",
  "bird-nature-sound-33-20953.mp3",
  "flowing-water-246403.mp3",
  "footsteps-in-water-nature-sounds-8185.mp3",
  "footsteps-on-nature-trail-246038.mp3",
  "heavy-rain-nature-sounds-8186.mp3",
  "nature-sound-near-river-or-waterfall-247409.mp3",
  "nature-sounds-240504.mp3",
  "quiet-nature-sounds-29791.mp3",
  "rain-sound-nature-sound-242838.mp3",
  "serbia-nature-sounds-245993.mp3",
  "sound-of-nature-deep-in-the-forests-10635.mp3",
  "thunder-245174.mp3"
]

# Preload all samples to avoid delays during playback
nature_samples.each do |sample_name|
  load_sample nature_path + sample_name
end

# Helper function to play preloaded nature sounds with variation
define :play_nature do |sample_name, rate=1, amp=0.7|
  full_path = nature_path + sample_name
  sample full_path, rate: rate, amp: amp
end

# Define a function for glitchy effects
define :glitch_effect do |sample_name, rate=1|
  with_fx :bitcrusher, bits: 8, sample_rate: 8000 do
    play_nature(sample_name, rate)
  end
end

# Define a function for ambient texture
define :background_texture do |sample_name|
  play_nature(sample_name, rate: rrand(0.75, 1.25), amp: 0.5)
end

# Ambient pad loop using preloaded nature sounds
live_loop :ambient_pads do
  play_nature("quiet-nature-sounds-29791.mp3", amp: 0.5)
  sleep 8
  play_nature("flowing-water-246403.mp3", amp: 0.5)
  sleep 8
end

# Beat loop with cautious rate adjustments
live_loop :beats do
  sync :ambient_pads
  # Removed extreme rate changes to prevent errors
  play_nature("heavy-rain-nature-sounds-8186.mp3", rate: 1, amp: 0.7)
  sleep 8
end

# Glitchy melody loop using bird sounds
live_loop :glitch_melody do
  sync :ambient_pads
  use_random_seed 300

  8.times do
    glitch_effect("bird-nature-sound-33-20953.mp3", rrand(0.75, 1.25))
    sleep [0.25, 0.5, 0.75].choose
  end
end

# Additional background texture
live_loop :background do
  sync :ambient_pads
  background_texture("nature-sounds-240504.mp3")
  sleep 8
end

# Subtle rhythmic glitches with preloaded nature samples
live_loop :rhythmic_glitches do
  sync :ambient_pads
  play_nature("footsteps-on-nature-trail-246038.mp3", rate: rrand(0.9, 1.1), amp: 0.3) if one_in(3)
  sleep [0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1].choose
end

# Soft pad progression with preloaded nature sounds
live_loop :soft_pads do
  sync :ambient_pads
  play_nature("nature-sound-near-river-or-waterfall-247409.mp3", amp: 0.5)
  sleep 4
  play_nature("nature-sounds-240504.mp3", amp: 0.5)
  sleep 4
end

  "sound-of-nature-deep-in-the-forests-10635.mp3",
  "thunder-245174.mp3"
]

# Preload all samples to avoid delays during playback
nature_samples.each do |sample_name|
  load_sample nature_path + sample_name
end

# Helper function to play preloaded nature sounds with variation
define :play_nature do |sample_name, rate=1, amp=0.7|
  full_path = nature_path + sample_name
  sample full_path, rate: rate, amp: amp
end

# Define a function for glitchy effects
define :glitch_effect do |sample_name, rate=1|
  with_fx :bitcrusher, bits: 8, sample_rate: 8000 do
    play_nature(sample_name, rate)
  end
end

# Define a function for ambient texture
define :background_texture do |sample_name|
  play_nature(sample_name, rate: rrand(0.75, 1.25), amp: 0.5)
end

  play_nature("quiet-nature-sounds-29791.mp3", amp: 0.5)
  sleep 8

  sleep 8

metadata.prompt:
REVIEW: “Under Ice, Summer Tape”

Under Ice is barely interested in behaving like an animal recording. Its opening minutes are all negative space: submerged room-tone, pressure, distant movement. Then the voices arrive—alien tonal bursts, startlingly un-mammalian in character, rounded notes suddenly splitting into metallic chirps and electronic-sounding sweeps.

Removed from any visible source, the performance becomes almost synth music. Long tones hover, bend and disappear; shorter calls answer from apparently impossible distances. The recording’s greatest strength is its refusal to organize the environment for us. The microphone hears indiscriminately, catching the desired voices alongside everything the human listener might have filtered away.

That ambiguity gives Under Ice its strange depth. Is the low wash accompaniment? Is the scrape percussion? Is the next rising tone one performer answering another, or merely something entering the hydrophone’s field?

By the end, source identification feels beside the point. The record has taught you to listen to the water itself as the ensemble.

FIELD NOTE 26-0719-B
Site: indoor amplified performance, northern England
Participants: “Brindle Group,” four persons
Observer position: rear-left of room

20:14 — Group begins with angular amplified string pattern. Principal male vocal speech-song, sardonic delivery. Drum set establishes continuous forward pulse.

20:18 — Keyboard enters intermittently rather than functioning as harmonic bed; piano appears to “wander” between guitar figures. Rhythm subsequently incorporates material resembling funk/dance-rock. Ensemble synchronization noticeably close; transitions appear jointly cued rather than directed by vocalist.

20:23 — Faster item. Muscular guitar figure + driving drums. Audience joins recurrent refrain. Performance intensity increases although verbal material remains comparatively simple. Each instrumental entrance appears to push the following part forward.

20:31 — Contrasting item: unhurried rhythm, understated guitars, dreamy piano phrases. Electronic layer audible beneath ensemble but not foregrounded. General motion experienced as gliding rather than surging.

20:37 — Repetitive refrain in later item does not develop substantially. Observer notes decrease in perceived distinctiveness despite continued physical intensity.

General: ensemble alternates wiry attack with unexpectedly open melodic passages; rhythmic motion often carries equal structural weight to text.

FIELD RECORDING LOG: N-14
Location: enclosed rehearsal structure; Pacific Northwest
Participants: ensemble “Ash Choir”
Weather: rain audible intermittently outside
Duration observed: c.45 min.

00:00–06:20 — Distorted string instruments employ continuous tremolo picking; percussion includes repeated high-speed kick and blastbeat figures. Little swing observed. Pitch inflection comparatively rigid.

06:21 — Tempo perception changes to near-dirge although kick drum remains highly active. Participants maintain intensity through density rather than apparent speed.

14:03 — Earlier death-march figure discontinued. Replaced by markedly grooving repeated riff. Two lead strings subsequently perform simultaneous rapid solos; texture temporarily destabilized.

27:40 — Low orange-toned synthesizer pulse introduced and held near center of texture. Affect judged markedly solitary/melancholic.

31:12 — Flute and acoustic guitar surround distorted principal riff; sustained keyboard line rises through texture. Rhythm lilting relative to preceding material.

39:05 — Recorded fire/crackle audible behind hand drums and acoustic strings. Mournful flute enters. Combination changes otherwise processional material toward rougher, more acrid texture.

General observation: participants repeatedly interrupt a highly restricted stylistic vocabulary with acoustic, environmental and archaizing sounds without abandoning the dominant performance grammar.

“Muddy Waters – 29. (Head of the house) Farms 16 acres. Been knowing Son House since ’29. Learned how to play with bottle neck from him”

“The power of the Spirit was so great upon me that I was obliged to call out, as in agony, for pardon and forgiveness and for strength to bear a faithful testimony. In these cryings I was, however, at the time conscious of a power of utterance carrying me beyond the natural expression of my feelings…. for the space of more than ten minutes I was, as it were, paralysed under a shaking of my limbs, my knees rapping one against the other, and no expression except a sort of convulsive sigh. During this period I had no other consciousness than this bodily emotion, and an inexpressible constraint upon my mind, which although it left me composed and sensible of all I was doing, yet prevented my utterance and gave no distinct impression, beyond a desire to pray for the knowledge of the Lord's will. This increased so much that I was led to fall on my knees and cry in a loud voice "Speak! Lord!"

Foochow stank of fish rot, coal smoke, and old piss. The alleys steamed. Dogs nosed at gristle-piles while laundry hissed overhead like lines of prayer flags. Li Wu stepped off the river ferry into that reek with a slight stoop in his shoulders—not from age or weakness, but habit. A man who listened first, moved second. His left hand toyed with the thumb-worn edge of his amber prayer beads, tucked half-concealed in his sleeve.

The foreigners had arrived two days prior, dragging crates stamped with stars and Latin abbreviations, tall under their fedoras, their language hard-edged and quick. Americans, someone had muttered at the dock, as if naming a species. A local fixer—one of the fat ones with government friends—had mentioned they needed a cook. Or a translator. Or both. It was never clear.

Li Wu wasn’t sure why he’d come. He told himself it was for the pay.

The tea shop they used as an interview room reeked of fried oil and scorched mint. Its windows were crusted with fly droppings, and someone had nailed half a Buddhist charm to the lintel. Superstition for prosperity, badly placed. A Western woman sat in the far corner, photographing a chipped bowl as if it were a Ming relic. Beside her, a man with angular shoulders and a field notebook tapped his pen on the edge of the table, rhythmically, like he was counting down.

Roy Chapman Andrews, Li Wu had learned. Spoke with the confidence of someone used to commanding rooms, but his Mandarin came out like wind-blown gravel. He asked questions as if they were levers.

Li Wu stood when called, and bowed faintly—neither servile nor stiff.

"Y-you r-r-require a man f-familiar w-w-with… city a-and i-inland d-dialects?" he said, each stumble carefully spaced, like stones set to slow pursuit.

Roy blinked. "Jesus. They weren't kidding. That stutter—well. Let’s see what you know. Where’s your English from?"

"Mission… school. K-Kunyang." He lifted his eyes slightly. "And… b-by w-w-work."

“You worked for Westerners?”

Li Wu gave a small nod. “S-some geologists. Missiona—missionaries. P-professors.”

Andrews turned to the woman—Yvette, the camera-woman, though no one had introduced her formally. She said nothing. Just tilted her head, observing. Li Wu noticed how her hand shifted to take notes—except she wasn’t writing. Only the muscle of it moved, lightly.

Roy grunted. “You know how to cook?”

“W-well enough to k-k-keep a w-white man’s st-stomach f-from c-c-collapsing, yes.”

That made the American bark a laugh. “Hell of a job description.”

They made him read a letter next, one written in formal French. A reference, maybe. Li Wu read it aloud in Mandarin, then again in passable English. He omitted the insulting metaphor tucked between the lines—“obedient as a trained macaque”—because he’d already decided it wasn’t worth anyone’s time. The woman noticed anyway. Her brow twitched, just barely. She knew.

Roy closed his notebook. “You’ll ride upriver with us, Li Wu. We leave at dawn. You’ll be cook, translator, and when required, the man who keeps the rest of us from walking straight into a clan feud.” He gestured vaguely. “Wages every three weeks. Room, rations, some extra if we make it west.”

A lesser man might’ve bowed low. Li Wu inclined his head, hands folded. "Th-thank you. I—I underst-stand."

Later, alone in the back courtyard of the guesthouse they’d assigned him, he sat under a skeletal loquat tree, watching smoke rise from the kitchens. A boy chopped fish heads. A pig screamed somewhere in a slaughter alley, cut off mid-wail. In the dusk light, Foochow shimmered. Not with beauty exactly—but with something stranger. Multiplicity. Rot and wonder. Piss and prayer.

Li Wu rubbed the edge of his pen—steel-nibbed, lacquer-repaired—and stared at the ink pooling in his thoughts. He’d been hired. Not seen, not yet. But he would be.

Scene 2

The steamer wheezed against the current like an asthmatic mule, dragging itself upriver through brown water thick with ash from the hills. The Min twisted through velvet-green slopes, sheer and shivering in the heat, but Li Wu kept his eyes on the deck—on boots and baskets, on crates tied with wire, on where the ropes bled rust into the planks. He crouched low, cleaning a brass rice pot with coarse salt and duck feathers. The motion soothed his tongue.

A crewman hacked and spat. Somewhere below, a child cried—then fell silent, too suddenly.

Three foreign crates had shifted during the night—one of them labeled “Dry Plates. Glass. Fragile.” He’d retied them himself before sunrise, using fisherman’s knots his father taught him as a boy, when they still lived near salt flats and the gods hadn’t yet gone silent.

From the upper deck, laughter rang out—bright, distant. The American woman. Li Wu didn’t turn to look, but he heard her shutter click: twice, then a pause. Then three more.

Roy Chapman Andrews paced behind her like a mastiff on a lead. Always moving, always explaining something to someone. He wore that wide-brimmed h

The background consists of a subtle, low-frequency synth drone and occasional high-frequency atmospheric textures. The vocal is dry with minimal room reverb, placed forward in the mix.
